cards.subject: Infrastructure as a service
says: rents virtual machines, storage and networks that the customer configures
leaves the guest operating system and everything above it to the customer
gives the customer the most control of the three classic service models
cards.use: need full control of the operating system and the software installed on it
not: hides the operating system and runtime from the customer

cards.subject: Platform as a service
says: runs customer application code without the customer managing servers or the operating system
patches the runtime and handles scaling on the customer's behalf
trades some control for less operational work
cards.use: want to push code and let the platform run it
not: gives the customer root access to the underlying host

cards.subject: Software as a service
says: delivers a finished application over the internet
leaves the customer to manage only users, configuration and their own data
needs no installation or servers from the customer
cards.use: need a ready-made business tool such as email or a CRM without running anything
not: lets the customer choose the operating system it runs on

cards.subject: Function as a service
says: runs short pieces of code in response to events
scales to zero when no events arrive
is billed by how much code actually executes rather than by idle servers
cards.use: have spiky, event-driven work and no wish to keep a server idle
not: keeps a dedicated server warm between requests by design

cards.subject: A public cloud
says: shares provider-owned data centres among many customers on demand
lets customers rent capacity with no hardware purchase
isolates tenants logically rather than by giving each its own building
cards.use: want capacity on demand without owning hardware
not: dedicates all hardware to a single organisation

cards.subject: A hybrid cloud
says: connects on-premises infrastructure with a public cloud
lets workloads and data move between the two environments
needs reliable network links and consistent identity across both sides
cards.use: must keep some systems on site while using cloud services for the rest
not: uses two different public providers at once

cards.subject: Multi-cloud
says: uses more than one public cloud provider
lowers dependence on a single vendor
raises operational complexity and the range of skills a team needs
cards.use: want to avoid reliance on one provider or use a service only another provider offers
not: keeps some systems on site and others in the cloud

cards.subject: Vendor lock-in
says: makes leaving a provider costly because of proprietary services and data formats
grows as more provider-specific managed services are adopted
is reduced by open standards and portable tooling, though never to zero
cards.use: weigh the convenience of a proprietary managed service against future portability
not: is removed entirely by running on virtual machines

cards.subject: A landing zone
says: provides a pre-configured, multi-account cloud baseline with guardrails
sets up shared identity, logging and networking before teams deploy workloads
lets new accounts start compliant instead of being hardened afterwards
cards.use: onboard many teams and want each to start from a secure, consistent base
not: is a single virtual machine image used by all teams

cards.subject: The shared responsibility model
says: splits security duties between the cloud provider and the customer
moves the dividing line depending on the service model used
never leaves the customer with zero responsibility
cards.use: need to decide who must patch, configure or monitor a layer
not: makes the provider responsible for the customer's data and access settings

cards.subject: Security of the cloud
says: covers the physical data centres, hosts and virtualisation layer
is the provider's duty under the shared responsibility model
is evidenced to customers through independent audit reports
cards.use: ask who protects the buildings and hypervisors
not: covers how a customer configures their own storage buckets

cards.subject: Security in the cloud
says: covers the customer's data, identities, access settings and configuration
stays with the customer in every service model
includes deciding who may read a storage bucket
cards.use: ask who must set permissions and protect the data
not: is handled entirely by the provider on managed services

cards.subject: Guest operating system patching
says: is the customer's job on infrastructure-as-a-service virtual machines
passes to the provider when the customer uses a platform or serverless service
leaves known vulnerabilities open if the customer ignores it
cards.use: run virtual machines and must keep their operating system current
not: is always done by the provider whatever service model is chosen

cards.subject: A publicly exposed storage bucket
says: is usually a customer configuration error rather than a provider failure
lets anyone with the address read the contents
is prevented by account-wide block-public-access guardrails
cards.use: investigate a data leak from cloud storage
not: happens only when the provider's data centre is breached

cards.subject: Encryption at rest
says: protects stored data if the underlying disks or backups are accessed
is applied to volumes, buckets and databases
is separate from protecting data while it travels
cards.use: worry about stolen disks or leaked backups
not: protects data while it crosses the network

cards.subject: Customer-managed keys
says: let the customer control the lifecycle of the key that encrypts provider-stored data
allow access to be cut off by disabling the key
add key-rotation and permission duties to the customer
cards.use: must prove you can revoke the provider's access to your data
not: remove the need to protect the key at all

cards.subject: A virtual machine
says: emulates a complete computer with its own operating system on shared hardware
boots from an image and is billed while it runs
lets an existing application move to the cloud with few changes
cards.use: need to lift an existing application over unchanged
not: shares the host's operating system kernel with other guests

cards.subject: An auto scaling group
says: keeps the number of instances between a minimum and a maximum
replaces instances that fail their health check
adds or removes instances based on a metric or schedule
cards.use: need a fleet to grow under load and heal itself
not: resizes the CPU of one running instance in place

cards.subject: A spot instance
says: uses spare provider capacity at a discount
can be reclaimed with short notice
suits fault-tolerant, interruptible work
cards.use: run a checkpointed batch job that can be restarted
not: is guaranteed to run until you stop it

cards.subject: A bare-metal server
says: gives one tenant the whole physical machine with no shared hypervisor
allows direct access to hardware features
suits licences tied to physical cores
cards.use: need direct hardware access or core-based licensing
not: is a virtual machine sharing a host with strangers

cards.subject: A serverless function
says: runs stateless code in response to an event
is started and scaled by the platform with no server to manage
has a time limit on each invocation
cards.use: want code to run only when an upload or message arrives
not: keeps local state on disk between invocations

cards.subject: A cold start
says: delays the first invocation while a fresh execution environment is prepared
adds latency to functions that have been idle
can be reduced by keeping some environments warm
cards.use: see occasional slow responses from a rarely used function
not: is a failure to restart a crashed server

cards.subject: Serverless containers
says: run container images without the customer managing nodes
scale with requests, often down to zero
suit stateless web services packaged as images
cards.use: have a containerised web service and no wish to run a cluster
not: require the customer to patch the host operating system

cards.subject: The instance metadata service
says: serves an instance's own details and temporary role credentials on a link-local address
is a target in server-side request forgery attacks
is hardened by requiring a session token before answering
cards.use: want an instance to read its role credentials without stored keys
not: is a public endpoint that lists every instance in the account

cards.subject: Object storage
says: stores data as objects addressed by a key in a flat namespace
is accessed through an HTTP API rather than mounted as a disk
scales to very large amounts of data without managing volumes
cards.use: keep user uploads, backups or static website assets
not: is mounted as a disk and formatted with a file system

cards.subject: Block storage
says: presents a raw volume that the operating system formats like a disk
is normally attached to one instance at a time
gives low-latency reads and writes suited to databases and boot disks
cards.use: need a fast disk for a database server
not: is addressed by object keys over HTTP

cards.subject: File storage
says: shares a network file system that many servers can mount at once
supports ordinary directories and file locking
suits applications that expect a shared path
cards.use: need several servers to read and write the same directory tree
not: is attached to exactly one instance at a time

cards.subject: A bucket
says: is the named top-level container that holds objects
carries its own access policy and settings
cannot be nested inside another bucket
cards.use: need a place to group objects with one access policy
not: is a disk volume attached to a server

cards.subject: A volume snapshot
says: captures a point-in-time copy of a block volume
is stored independently of the instance it came from
can be used to create a new volume
cards.use: need a restorable copy of a disk before a risky change
not: keeps updating itself as the volume changes

cards.subject: Object versioning
says: keeps earlier versions of an object after it is overwritten or deleted
lets an accidentally deleted object be restored
increases storage use because old versions are kept
cards.use: want to undo an accidental overwrite of a stored file
not: compresses objects to save space

cards.subject: A storage lifecycle rule
says: moves or expires objects automatically as they age
cuts cost by shifting cold data to cheaper classes
can delete incomplete uploads and old versions
cards.use: want logs to move to cold storage after a month and be deleted after a year
not: encrypts objects when they are first written

cards.subject: A presigned URL
says: grants time-limited access to one private object
avoids sharing the account's credentials
stops working once its expiry passes
cards.use: let a browser upload or download one private file directly
not: makes the whole bucket public

cards.subject: A virtual private cloud
says: provides a logically isolated virtual network with its own address range
contains subnets, route tables and gateways
is where most cloud resources are placed
cards.use: need a private network for your cloud resources
not: is a physical network in the provider's building

cards.subject: A subnet
says: divides a virtual network's address range into a smaller block
is usually tied to a single availability zone
is public or private depending on its routes
cards.use: want to separate tiers of an application inside one network
not: spans several regions at once

cards.subject: A public subnet
says: has a route to an internet gateway
hosts internet-facing load balancers or bastion hosts
needs instances to hold public addresses to be reached directly
cards.use: place a load balancer that must be reachable from the internet
not: has no route to the internet at all

cards.subject: A private subnet
says: has no direct inbound route from the internet
hosts databases and application servers
reaches the internet only through a NAT gateway or endpoint
cards.use: place a database that only the application should reach
not: is the place for the internet-facing load balancer

cards.subject: A NAT gateway
says: lets private resources start outbound connections to the internet
blocks unsolicited inbound connections
translates private addresses to a public one
cards.use: let private servers download updates without being reachable
not: makes private instances directly reachable from the internet

cards.subject: A route table
says: decides where traffic from a subnet is sent based on its destination
contains a local route for the network's own addresses
is associated with one or more subnets
cards.use: send traffic for an on-premises range through a VPN
not: filters traffic by allowing or denying ports

cards.subject: A private endpoint
says: gives a managed service a private address inside your network
keeps traffic off the public internet
lets access be limited to the network that holds the endpoint
cards.use: reach a storage service without sending traffic across the internet
not: opens the service to the whole internet

cards.subject: A security group
says: acts as a stateful firewall attached to a resource's network interface
allows return traffic for an allowed connection automatically
is typically written as allow rules rather than deny rules
cards.use: limit a database to connections from the application servers
not: is stateless and needs a rule for return traffic

cards.subject: A network ACL
says: filters traffic at the subnet boundary
is stateless, so return traffic needs its own rule
evaluates numbered rules in order and can deny
cards.use: add a coarse subnet-wide deny for a hostile address range
not: tracks connections so replies are allowed automatically

cards.subject: An application load balancer
says: routes requests by host name, path or header
terminates TLS and understands HTTP
can send different paths to different backend groups
cards.use: route /api and /static to different services
not: forwards raw TCP without reading HTTP

cards.subject: An access policy
says: lists which actions are allowed or denied on which resources
attaches to an identity or a resource
is a document evaluated on every request
cards.use: grant read-only access to one bucket
not: stores the password for an account

cards.subject: An IAM role
says: grants temporary permissions to whoever assumes it
has no long-lived password or key of its own
is assumed by people, services or workloads
cards.use: give a virtual machine access to storage without storing keys
not: is a fixed login with a permanent password

cards.subject: A long-lived access key
says: is a static credential that stays valid until rotated or deleted
is often leaked through code repositories
should be replaced by roles where possible
cards.use: find a credential that was committed to a repository
not: expires automatically after a few hours

cards.subject: Temporary credentials
says: expire automatically after a short period
are issued when a role is assumed
limit the damage if they leak
cards.use: grant a build job access for the duration of one run
not: remain valid until someone deletes them

cards.subject: Workload identity
says: lets a running workload obtain cloud credentials from its platform identity
removes the need to store a secret in the application
ties permissions to the workload rather than to a person
cards.use: let a pod call a cloud API with no stored key
not: relies on a shared admin password in an environment variable

cards.subject: A permission boundary
says: caps the maximum permissions an identity can ever be granted
applies even when attached policies grant more
lets delegated admins create roles without exceeding a limit
cards.use: allow developers to create roles but never beyond a set ceiling
not: grants permissions to an identity

cards.subject: A privilege escalation path
says: lets a limited identity gain more rights through permitted actions
often arises from permission to attach policies or pass roles
is found by reviewing which permissions can modify permissions
cards.use: review whether a developer role can make itself an administrator
not: is an authorised increase approved in a ticket

cards.subject: A managed relational database
says: automates patching, backups and failover for a SQL engine
leaves schema design and query tuning to the customer
does not normally give the customer access to the host operating system
cards.use: want a SQL database without administering the server
not: lets the customer log in to the host as root

cards.subject: A read replica
says: serves read queries from a copy of the primary's data
lags the primary slightly because it replicates asynchronously
scales reads but not writes
cards.use: relieve a primary database overloaded by reporting queries
not: accepts writes that are merged back automatically

cards.subject: Point-in-time recovery
says: restores a database to any moment within the retention window
works by replaying logged changes on top of a backup
is the way to undo a bad delete issued minutes ago
cards.use: recover from an accidental DELETE without a WHERE clause
not: restores only the most recent nightly backup

cards.subject: A managed NoSQL store
says: scales horizontally by spreading items across partitions
trades joins and flexible queries for scale and speed
is queried mainly by key
cards.use: need huge throughput with simple lookups by key
not: supports arbitrary multi-table joins by design

cards.subject: An in-memory cache
says: keeps hot data in RAM to cut latency and database load
can lose its contents on restart
needs an expiry or invalidation strategy
cards.use: serve repeated reads faster than the database can
not: is the durable system of record

cards.subject: A message queue
says: holds each message until one consumer processes it
decouples how fast producers send from how fast consumers work
smooths bursts of work
cards.use: let a web request hand slow work to background workers
not: delivers every message to all subscribers at once

cards.subject: A dead-letter queue
says: collects messages that repeatedly fail processing
keeps poison messages from blocking the main queue
lets engineers inspect and replay failures
cards.use: stop one malformed message from being retried forever
not: is where successfully processed messages are archived

cards.subject: At-least-once delivery
says: may deliver a message more than once
requires consumers to be idempotent
is a common default in queues
cards.use: design a consumer that must not charge a customer twice
not: guarantees exactly one delivery with no duplicates

cards.subject: A region
says: is a geographic area containing several data centres
is chosen for latency, data residency and available services
keeps its services independent of other regions
cards.use: decide where to place a workload near its users
not: is a single data centre room

cards.subject: An availability zone
says: is one or more isolated data centres inside a region
has independent power, cooling and networking
is linked to its siblings by fast, low-latency networks
cards.use: spread a service so one building failure does not stop it
not: is a separate country-level region

cards.subject: A multi-zone deployment
says: spreads instances across availability zones
survives the loss of one zone
needs a load balancer to share traffic between zones
cards.use: want a service to survive a data centre outage
not: protects against the loss of an entire region

cards.subject: Active-passive failover
says: keeps a standby environment in a second region
sends traffic there only after the primary fails
costs less than running both regions at once
cards.use: want regional disaster recovery without double running cost
not: serves users from both regions simultaneously

cards.subject: Active-active
says: serves users from several regions at the same time
must resolve data replication conflicts
gives the fastest recovery when one region fails
cards.use: need near-zero downtime across regional failure
not: keeps the second region idle until a disaster

cards.subject: Recovery time objective
says: states how long a service may be down after a failure
guides how much to spend on standby capacity
is measured in time to restore service
cards.use: agree with the business how fast service must return
not: states how much recent data may be lost

cards.subject: Recovery point objective
says: states how much recent data may be lost, measured in time
drives how often data is backed up or replicated
is near zero only with continuous replication
cards.use: agree how much work could be lost in a disaster
not: states how long the outage may last

cards.subject: A backup
says: is a separate point-in-time copy used to recover from deletion or corruption
lets you return to a state before a mistake
should be tested by restoring it
cards.use: need to undo corruption that happened last week
not: mirrors every change instantly, including mistakes

cards.subject: Replication
says: copies changes continuously to another location
improves availability and read capacity
propagates a deletion or corruption too
cards.use: keep a second copy ready for failover
not: lets you roll back to last Tuesday

cards.subject: A pod
says: is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes
groups one or more containers that share a network address and volumes
is replaced rather than repaired when it fails
cards.use: need containers to run together and share localhost
not: is a physical or virtual machine in the cluster

cards.subject: A deployment
says: manages ReplicaSets to roll out and roll back changes to stateless pods
declares the desired number of replicas
supports rolling updates by default
cards.use: run a stateless web app with several replicas and safe updates
not: gives each pod a stable identity and its own volume

cards.subject: A service
says: gives a set of pods a stable virtual address and DNS name
selects pods by label and balances traffic across them
keeps working as pods come and go
cards.use: let other workloads reach pods whose IP addresses change
not: routes external HTTP requests by host and path

cards.subject: An ingress
says: routes external HTTP and HTTPS requests to services by host and path
needs an ingress controller to take effect
can terminate TLS for several hosts
cards.use: expose several web services behind one entry point
not: gives pods a cluster-internal virtual address

cards.subject: A config map
says: holds non-secret configuration as key-value data
is injected as environment variables or files
lets the same image run with different settings
cards.use: change an app setting without rebuilding the image
not: is intended for passwords and tokens

cards.subject: A stateful set
says: gives each pod a stable name and its own persistent volume
starts and stops pods in a defined order
suits databases and other clustered stateful software
cards.use: run a clustered database whose members need fixed identities
not: treats all pods as interchangeable

cards.subject: A persistent volume claim
says: requests storage for a pod without naming the underlying disk
is matched to a persistent volume or created from a storage class
keeps data when the pod is rescheduled
cards.use: give a pod storage that outlives it
not: is a temporary scratch directory deleted with the pod

cards.subject: A network policy
says: restricts which pods may talk to which
takes effect only if the network plugin enforces it
moves a namespace from open to default-deny when applied
cards.use: allow only the web tier to reach the database pods
not: encrypts traffic between pods

cards.subject: The control plane
says: makes global decisions and holds the cluster's desired state
includes the API server, scheduler and controllers
does not normally run the application workloads
cards.use: ask which part of the cluster decides where pods run
not: runs on every worker node to start containers

cards.subject: A node
says: is a worker machine that runs pods
runs a kubelet and a container runtime
is virtual or physical
cards.use: ask which machines actually run the pods
not: is the component that schedules pods

cards.subject: A reconciliation loop
says: compares the desired state with the observed state
acts to close any difference it finds
is how controllers heal failed pods
cards.use: explain why a deleted pod comes back by itself
not: applies each change once and never checks again

cards.subject: A readiness probe
says: tells Kubernetes when a pod can receive traffic
removes a failing pod from service endpoints without restarting it
keeps traffic away while the app is still starting
cards.use: hold traffic back until the app has loaded its data
not: restarts the container when it fails

cards.subject: A liveness probe
says: tells Kubernetes whether a container is stuck and needs a restart
causes the kubelet to restart the container on repeated failure
should not depend on slow downstream services
cards.use: restart a container that has deadlocked
not: only removes the pod from load balancing

cards.subject: A resource request
says: tells the scheduler how much CPU and memory a container needs
is used to decide which node has room
is the basis for autoscaling on utilisation
cards.use: help the scheduler place pods on nodes with enough capacity
not: kills the container when usage goes above it

cards.subject: A resource limit
says: caps the CPU or memory a container may use
throttles CPU use above the limit
gets a container killed when it exceeds its memory limit
cards.use: stop one container from starving its neighbours
not: only influences where the pod is scheduled

cards.subject: An operator
says: encodes an application's operational knowledge in a custom controller
manages custom resources such as a database cluster
automates tasks such as backup and failover
cards.use: automate the day-two operation of a complex stateful application
not: is a human on-call engineer

cards.subject: A Dockerfile
says: lists the instructions for building a container image
is read from top to bottom, each instruction forming a step
starts with a FROM line naming the base image
cards.use: need a repeatable recipe for an image
not: is the running container itself

cards.subject: A base image
says: supplies the starting filesystem and tools for a new image
is named in the FROM instruction
determines much of an image's size and attack surface
cards.use: choose what a new image is built on
not: is the registry where images are stored

cards.subject: A multi-stage build
says: uses several FROM stages in one Dockerfile
copies only the needed outputs into the final image
keeps compilers and build tools out of the runtime image
cards.use: ship a small image without the build toolchain
not: runs several containers at once

cards.subject: An image tag
says: is a human-readable label that points at an image version
can be moved to a different image later
is not a guarantee of identical content over time
cards.use: refer to a build such as 1.4 or latest
not: is a content hash that never changes

cards.subject: An image digest
says: is a content hash that identifies exactly one image
never points at different content
lets a deployment pin the exact bytes that were tested
cards.use: make sure production runs the very image that passed testing
not: can be re-pointed at a new build

cards.subject: A container registry
says: stores and serves container images by repository and tag
is where build pipelines push and nodes pull
can enforce access control and scanning
cards.use: share an image between a build job and the servers that run it
not: runs the containers it stores

cards.subject: A Linux namespace
says: isolates what a process can see, such as processes, network or mounts
is one of the kernel features that makes containers possible
limits visibility rather than resource use
cards.use: explain why a container sees its own process list
not: caps the memory a process may use

cards.subject: A control group
says: limits and accounts for the CPU, memory and I/O a set of processes can use
is the kernel feature behind container resource limits
is what ends a container that exceeds its memory limit
cards.use: explain how a container is held to a memory limit
not: hides other processes from view

cards.subject: Docker Compose
says: defines and runs several containers from one YAML file
creates networks and volumes for the services it declares
suits a single host better than a large cluster
cards.use: run an app, its database and a cache together on one machine
not: schedules containers across a fleet of nodes

cards.subject: A rootless container
says: runs the container engine and containers without root privileges on the host
limits the damage of a container escape
has restrictions around low ports and some storage features
cards.use: reduce the impact if an attacker breaks out of a container
not: gives the container full root on the host

cards.subject: HCL
says: is the configuration language used to write Terraform
describes resources in blocks with arguments
is declarative rather than a script of commands
cards.use: read or write a Terraform file
not: is a state storage service

cards.subject: A Terraform provider
says: is a plugin that talks to an external API such as a cloud
defines the resource types that can be managed
is downloaded during terraform init
cards.use: manage resources of a particular cloud or service
not: is the file that records what exists

cards.subject: A Terraform resource
says: declares one infrastructure object to be created and managed
is identified by its type and name
is changed by editing its arguments and applying
cards.use: declare a bucket or server in code
not: only reads information about existing objects

cards.subject: An input variable
says: lets a configuration or module take values from outside
can have a type, a default and a description
avoids hard-coding values that differ per environment
cards.use: use the same code for staging and production with different sizes
not: exposes a result to other configurations

cards.subject: The Terraform state file
says: records the real objects mapped to the configuration
is how Terraform knows what to change
can contain sensitive values in plain text
cards.use: understand why Terraform knows an object already exists
not: is the configuration you write by hand

cards.subject: A remote backend
says: stores the state in shared storage rather than on one laptop
lets a team work from the same state
commonly supports encryption and access control
cards.use: let several engineers and a pipeline share one state
not: keeps state in a local file in the working directory

cards.subject: A Terraform plan
says: previews the changes Terraform would make
compares configuration, state and real infrastructure
changes nothing by itself
cards.use: review a change before it touches production
not: creates the resources immediately

cards.subject: Terraform apply
says: carries out the changes in a plan
updates the state with the results
can be run from a saved plan so exactly what was reviewed is applied
cards.use: make the reviewed changes real
not: only shows what would happen

cards.subject: A Terraform module
says: packages a group of resources for reuse
takes input variables and returns outputs
reduces repetition between environments
cards.use: reuse the same network layout in several environments
not: is a single resource definition

cards.subject: Configuration drift
says: is when real infrastructure no longer matches the declared code
is often caused by manual changes in the console
is revealed by a plan that shows unexpected changes
cards.use: notice a firewall rule edited by hand outside the code
not: is a deliberate change made through the pipeline

cards.subject: The for_each argument
says: creates one instance per element of a map or set
keys instances by name so removing one leaves the others alone
avoids index shifting
cards.use: create several buckets from a named collection safely
not: creates a fixed number of identical copies indexed by position

cards.subject: The Terraform moved block
says: records that a resource has been renamed or relocated in code
lets Terraform update the state instead of destroying and recreating
helps refactor into modules safely
cards.use: rename a resource without replacing it
not: imports a resource from outside

cards.subject: A CI runner
says: is the machine or container that executes a pipeline job
picks up queued jobs from the CI service
provides the environment the job's steps run in
cards.use: ask where the build commands actually execute
not: is the file that defines the pipeline

cards.subject: A workflow file
says: defines a pipeline as triggers, jobs and steps in YAML
lives in the repository alongside the code
is stored under .github/workflows for GitHub Actions
cards.use: change what the pipeline does through a pull request
not: is the machine that runs the jobs

cards.subject: A provider-hosted runner
says: is a fresh virtual machine supplied and maintained by the CI provider
needs no server administration by the team
is discarded after the job
cards.use: avoid operating build machines
not: is a machine the team installs and patches itself

cards.subject: A self-hosted runner
says: runs on machines the team owns and maintains
can reach private networks and use special hardware
becomes a security risk if untrusted code runs on it
cards.use: build on hardware inside a private network
not: is created fresh by the provider for every job

cards.subject: An ephemeral runner
says: handles one job and is destroyed afterwards
stops state or secrets leaking from one job to the next
is the safer pattern for self-hosted fleets
cards.use: prevent a malicious job from leaving a backdoor on the build machine
not: is reused for many jobs so caches stay warm

cards.subject: A matrix build
says: runs the same job across combinations of values such as versions or operating systems
expands one definition into several parallel jobs
can fail fast or continue when one combination fails
cards.use: test a library on three runtime versions
not: runs different jobs in a fixed order

cards.subject: A build cache
says: stores downloaded dependencies or build outputs between runs
is looked up by a key built from files such as a lock file
speeds up pipelines but can serve stale content if keys are poor
cards.use: avoid downloading the same packages on every run
not: is the final deliverable of a build

cards.subject: OIDC authentication from CI
says: exchanges a short-lived token issued to the job for cloud credentials
removes the need to store long-lived cloud keys as secrets
lets the cloud restrict access to a specific repository and branch
cards.use: let a pipeline deploy without a stored access key
not: stores a permanent key in the repository settings

cards.subject: A concurrency group
says: allows only one run of a named set of workflows at a time
can queue or cancel older runs
prevents two deployments overlapping
cards.use: stop two deploys to the same environment running together
not: splits a job into parallel copies

cards.subject: Pinning an action to a commit SHA
says: fixes a third-party step to one exact version of its code
stops a moved tag from changing what runs
is a supply-chain protection for pipelines
cards.use: defend against a compromised third-party action tag
not: always uses the newest release automatically

cards.subject: A pull request from a fork
says: comes from code outside the repository's trust boundary
should not be given repository secrets by default
is a risk when a privileged trigger checks out the submitted code
cards.use: decide how much trust to give a contributor's workflow run
not: is always safe to run with full secrets

cards.subject: Prometheus
says: scrapes metrics from targets over HTTP on an interval
stores samples as time series identified by labels
is queried with PromQL
cards.use: collect numeric metrics from many services
not: indexes the full text of log lines

cards.subject: High cardinality
says: means a metric has very many distinct label combinations
inflates storage and memory use
is triggered by labels such as user ID or full URL
cards.use: explain why a metric labelled with the user ID overloads the system
not: makes queries faster by spreading them out

cards.subject: A counter metric
says: only increases, apart from resets to zero
is read as a rate over time rather than as a raw total
suits requests served and errors seen
cards.use: measure how many requests have been handled
not: goes up and down to show the current value

cards.subject: A histogram metric
says: counts observations in buckets of value ranges
lets percentiles be estimated from the buckets
can be aggregated across instances
cards.use: measure request latency distribution across many servers
not: records only a single current value

cards.subject: A latency percentile
says: states the value below which a given share of requests fall
shows tail latency that an average hides
cannot be correctly obtained by averaging per-server percentiles
cards.use: find how slow the slowest users' requests are
not: is the mean of all request times

cards.subject: Alertmanager
says: groups, deduplicates and routes alerts to receivers
applies silences and inhibition
does not evaluate the alerting rules itself
cards.use: send related alerts as one page to the on-call engineer
not: scrapes metrics from targets

cards.subject: Grafana
says: visualises data from many data sources in dashboards
does not store the metrics itself
can show metrics, logs and traces together
cards.use: build a dashboard over metrics and logs
not: is the database that holds the time series

cards.subject: Loki
says: indexes only the labels of log streams, not the full text
stores compressed log chunks cheaply
is queried with LogQL
cards.use: keep logs cheaply and find them by service and environment
not: builds a full-text index of every word

cards.subject: OpenTelemetry
says: is a vendor-neutral standard and toolkit for traces, metrics and logs
lets applications be instrumented once and exported to many backends
defines a common wire protocol
cards.use: instrument services without tying them to a monitoring vendor
not: is a single commercial monitoring product

cards.subject: Trace context propagation
says: passes trace identifiers between services in request headers
is what lets spans from different services join one trace
breaks if a service fails to forward the headers
cards.use: find why a trace stops at one service
not: samples a fraction of traces to save cost

cards.subject: A budget alert
says: notifies people when spend passes a set threshold
can fire on actual or forecast cost
warns but does not stop spending by itself
cards.use: get warned before a bill grows out of control
not: blocks all new resources at the threshold

cards.subject: Resource tagging
says: attaches key-value labels such as team or environment to resources
lets costs be grouped and attributed
works only if tags are applied consistently
cards.use: find out which team owns a cost
not: encrypts the labelled resource

cards.subject: Rightsizing
says: matches resource size to observed usage
cuts waste from over-provisioned servers
relies on utilisation metrics over a representative period
cards.use: shrink servers that run at a tiny fraction of capacity
not: buys a long-term commitment

cards.subject: A commitment discount
says: trades a promise of steady usage for a lower rate
suits stable baseline workloads
wastes money if the commitment goes unused
cards.use: cover the predictable base load of production
not: is the cheapest option for short experiments

cards.subject: Spot capacity
says: trades possible interruption for a lower rate
suits stateless or checkpointed work
is a poor fit for a single database server
cards.use: run fault-tolerant batch workers cheaply
not: is guaranteed to stay running

cards.subject: Data egress charges
says: bill for data leaving a provider or crossing regions
can make chatty cross-region designs costly
are reduced by keeping traffic close and caching at the edge
cards.use: explain a surprise bill from moving data between regions
not: apply to data uploaded into the cloud

cards.subject: Orphaned resources
says: are items such as unattached disks and old snapshots still billing
remain after the server that used them was deleted
are found by regular cleanup reviews
cards.use: explain why a bill stays high after servers were removed
not: are resources in active use by a running service

cards.subject: Unit cost
says: relates cloud spend to a business measure such as cost per order
shows whether efficiency is improving as the business grows
is more informative than total spend alone
cards.use: tell whether a rising bill is just growth in usage
not: is the price of a single virtual machine

cards.subject: PM2 on our VPS
says: restarts a Node app if it dies
brings the apps back after a reboot once pm2 save has been run
starts our Next.js apps behind the proxy
cards.use: want the apps to survive crashes and reboots on the production VPS
not: acts as the reverse proxy in front of the apps

cards.subject: Apache on our VPS
says: acts as the reverse proxy for the live apps
forwards requests to a local port with ProxyPass and ProxyPassReverse
also serves ggmoney's PHP
cards.use: ask which program receives public traffic on the production server
not: is the process manager that restarts the apps

cards.subject: Certbot on our VPS
says: obtains Let's Encrypt certificates
creates the port-443 vhost file
renews the certificates
cards.use: ask how the sites get and keep HTTPS certificates
not: manages the Node processes

cards.subject: gglearn's Cloudflare-only allow-list
says: is generated by update-cloudflare-ips.sh from Cloudflare's published address ranges
stops anyone bypassing Cloudflare and spoofing X-Forwarded-For
is refused by the script if the list looks implausible
cards.use: explain why only Cloudflare and the machine itself may connect to the origin
not: issues the TLS certificate for the site

cards.subject: gglearn's deploy workflow
says: runs on every push to main and can be started by hand
uses a concurrency group named deploy with cancel-in-progress set to false
runs no tests or lint
cards.use: ask what happens when someone pushes to main in gglearn
not: cancels a running deploy as soon as a newer push arrives

cards.subject: gglearn's post-deploy health poll
says: polls the local app up to ten times
fails the deploy if the app never returns 200
runs at the end of deploy.sh after pm2 save
cards.use: ask how gglearn's deploy notices a broken release
not: rolls the app back automatically

cards.subject: Moksy's moksy-internal network
says: is marked internal: true in Docker Compose
gives its containers no route to the outside world
is separate from moksy-public
cards.use: ask how Moksy keeps some containers off the internet
not: is the network that exposes services publicly

cards.subject: Moksy's restart policy
says: is restart: unless-stopped
brings back a process that exits with code 0
was chosen because on-failure would never restart a clean exit
cards.use: ask why a container that exits cleanly still comes back
not: restarts a container only after a non-zero exit

cards.subject: Moksy's dashboard image
says: is built in stages: a node stage compiles the Vite app
copies only the compiled dist into a small nginx image
uses nginx purely as a static file server in a container
cards.use: ask where we use Nginx
not: runs nginx as the reverse proxy on the VPS

cards.subject: Moksy's ci workflow
says: runs on pushes and pull requests with a real Mongo service container
includes a Compose config check and a Trivy image scan
also runs lint, unit, integration and smoke jobs
cards.use: ask what checks protect Moksy's main branch
not: builds images and pushes them to GHCR by hand

cards.subject: Moksy's k8s/base folder
says: holds a gateway Deployment, an autoscaler, an Ingress, a NetworkPolicy and a PodDisruptionBudget
exists as configuration with no sign that a cluster runs it
is not how Moksy is actually deployed today
cards.use: ask whether Moksy runs on Kubernetes
not: is the production deployment method for gglearn

cards.subject: Terraform in our repositories
says: is absent, because no .tf files exist in any repo searched
is named only as a catalogued Moksy integration
is not something we operate
cards.use: ask whether our infrastructure is managed with Terraform
not: is used to build the VPS for the Next.js apps

cards.subject: The run, configured, catalogued or absent rule
says: gives four honest answers to whether we use a tool
separates what runs from what only exists as config or as a listed integration
avoids claiming Kubernetes or Terraform as part of our stack
cards.use: are asked in an interview whether we use Kubernetes
not: says every tool in a repository folder is in production

qa.q: Which cloud service model leaves the customer responsible for the guest operating system?
qa.right: Infrastructure as a service
qa.why: With virtual machines the customer patches and configures the operating system; higher-level models move that to the provider.

qa.q: Which storage type suits user-uploaded images that are served over HTTP and never edited in place?
qa.right: Object storage
wrong: Block storage attached to a database server
qa.why: Object storage holds whole objects addressed by key and is accessed through an HTTP API.

qa.q: What is an availability zone?
qa.right: One or more isolated data centres within a region
wrong: A content delivery location near users
qa.why: Zones have independent power and networking and are connected by fast links inside a region.

qa.q: In a container Dockerfile, what does the FROM line specify?
qa.right: The base image the new image is built on
wrong: The command to run at start-up
qa.why: Every Dockerfile starts from a base image, named in FROM.

qa.q: A web tier must be reachable from the internet while the database must not be. Where should each be placed?
qa.right: Web tier in a public subnet, database in a private subnet
wrong: Both in a public subnet with a strict firewall
Web tier in a private subnet, database in a public subnet
Both in the same subnet with no rules
qa.why: Public subnets route to an internet gateway; private subnets have no direct inbound route.

qa.q: What does a Kubernetes service provide?
qa.right: A stable address and DNS name in front of a changing set of pods
wrong: A way to build container images
qa.why: Pods are replaced and change IP addresses; a service selects them by label and gives clients one stable endpoint.

qa.q: Which part of the shared responsibility model always stays with the customer?
qa.right: Their data, identities and access configuration
qa.why: The provider secures the cloud; the customer secures what they put in it.

qa.q: What is the main benefit of a CI runner being provider-hosted?
qa.right: The team does not have to build and patch the build machines
wrong: It can reach the team's private network by default
It keeps caches between all jobs forever
It is exempt from using secrets
qa.why: Hosted runners are maintained by the provider and are fresh for each job.

qa.q: What does Prometheus do by default to collect metrics?
qa.right: It scrapes HTTP endpoints on targets at an interval
wrong: Targets push every sample to it using email
It queries the database of each service
qa.why: Prometheus uses a pull model: it fetches metrics from each target.

qa.q: Which Kubernetes object suits a clustered database whose members need stable names and their own disks?
qa.right: StatefulSet
qa.why: A StatefulSet gives each pod a stable identity and its own persistent volume.

qa.q: A Deployment's pods keep being killed and restarted with the reason OOMKilled. What is the most likely cause?
qa.right: The container exceeded its memory limit
wrong: The service selector does not match any pod
qa.why: Exceeding a memory limit gets a container killed; a failed readiness probe only removes a pod from traffic.

qa.q: What is the main difference between a backup and replication?
qa.right: A backup is a separate point-in-time copy; replication copies changes continuously, including mistakes
wrong: Replication is slower and cheaper than a backup
A backup mirrors every change instantly
Replication can restore data from last week
qa.why: Replication propagates deletions and corruption, which is why it is not a substitute for backups.

qa.q: Why does a team add a NAT gateway to a VPC?
qa.right: So private instances can start outbound connections while staying unreachable from the internet
wrong: So the internet can reach private instances directly
qa.why: NAT lets private resources reach out, for example for updates, without inbound exposure.

qa.q: What distinguishes an image tag from an image digest?
qa.right: A tag can be moved to different content; a digest identifies exactly one image
wrong: A digest can be changed later; a tag cannot
A tag is a content hash; a digest is a label
They are two names for the same thing
qa.why: Tags are mutable labels; a digest is a content hash.

qa.q: Which is the best reason to use a multi-stage Docker build?
qa.right: Keep compilers and build tools out of the final runtime image
wrong: Run the container on several hosts
qa.why: Only the needed output is copied into the last stage, so the final image stays small and has fewer tools to abuse.

qa.q: A function-based service answers rarely used requests slowly the first time and quickly afterwards. What is this called?
qa.right: A cold start
qa.why: A fresh execution environment must be initialised for the first invocation after idle time.

qa.q: In Terraform, what does the state file let the tool do?
qa.right: Map the configuration to the real objects it manages
qa.why: Without state Terraform would not know which real objects belong to which resources.

qa.q: Why should Terraform state live in a remote backend with locking when a team applies changes?
qa.right: To share one state and stop two applies changing it at the same time
wrong: To avoid writing the configuration in code
qa.why: Local state is not shared, and concurrent applies could corrupt it.

qa.q: What is the effect of this workflow setting?
qa.right: Only one deploy runs at a time and a running deploy is not cancelled by a newer one
wrong: Every push cancels the running deploy
Deploys run in parallel for speed
The workflow is skipped on weekends
qa.why: The group name serialises runs; cancel-in-progress false keeps the running one.

qa.q: Which setting makes a Kubernetes container get throttled rather than killed when it uses too much CPU?
qa.right: A CPU limit
qa.why: CPU over the limit is throttled; memory over the limit gets the container killed.

qa.q: What does this IAM-style policy allow?
qa.right: Reading objects from one bucket, and nothing else
wrong: Reading every bucket in the account
qa.why: Only the GetObject action is allowed, on objects within that single bucket.

qa.q: What is the safest way for a CI job to deploy to a cloud account?
qa.right: Exchange the job's short-lived OIDC token for temporary cloud credentials
wrong: Store an admin access key as a repository secret
Commit a key file to a private repository
Run the job on the root account
qa.why: Federation removes long-lived keys and can be restricted to one repository and branch.

qa.q: What does a readiness probe failure do?
qa.right: Removes the pod from the service's endpoints without restarting it
wrong: Moves the pod to another namespace
qa.why: Readiness controls traffic; liveness controls restarts.

qa.q: A trace shows the front end and the first service, but the rest of the request is missing. What is the most likely cause?
qa.right: A service is not forwarding the trace context headers
wrong: The metrics have too many labels
The histogram buckets are too wide
qa.why: Context propagation joins spans across services; a break loses everything downstream.

qa.q: Why is averaging per-server 99th percentile latencies misleading?
qa.right: Percentiles cannot be combined by averaging; the result does not equal the overall percentile
wrong: The mean of percentiles is always higher
qa.why: You need to aggregate the underlying distributions, for example histogram buckets.

qa.q: What does a permission boundary do?
qa.right: Sets the maximum permissions an identity can have, whatever its policies grant
wrong: Replaces its password with a token
qa.why: It is a ceiling, not a grant.

qa.q: What does this Terraform block do?
qa.right: Refuses any plan that would destroy the database
wrong: Backs up the database before destroy
qa.why: prevent_destroy makes Terraform error on a plan that destroys the resource.

qa.q: A team's nightly job reads from the primary database and slows the website. What should they do first?
qa.right: Point the reporting job at a read replica
wrong: Add a second primary that accepts writes
Switch the database to object storage
Turn off backups during the day
qa.why: A read replica serves reads from a copy and keeps reporting load off the primary, accepting a little lag.

qa.q: A developer commits a cloud access key to a repository by mistake. What should they do first?
qa.right: Revoke or rotate the key, then remove it from use
wrong: Delete the commit and keep the key
Wait to see whether it is used
qa.why: A key in history must be treated as leaked; rotation ends its usefulness, and cleaning history alone does not.

qa.q: A team's website must stay up if one data centre building fails. What is the minimum design?
qa.right: Run instances in at least two availability zones behind a load balancer
wrong: Run two instances in one availability zone
Move the site to a larger instance
qa.why: Zones fail independently; instances in one zone share its fate.

qa.q: A pull request changes a Terraform security group. The plan also shows the production database will be destroyed and recreated. What should the reviewer do?
qa.right: Stop and find out why before anyone applies it
wrong: Approve because plan output is always right
Apply it, then check the data afterwards
Ignore it because the change is only a security group
qa.why: A surprise destroy usually means a renamed resource or changed immutable argument; investigate before applying.

qa.q: A pod stays in CrashLoopBackOff. Which command shows why it last exited?
qa.right: kubectl logs <pod> --previous
qa.why: The previous container's logs usually show the crash cause.

qa.q: A service's p99 latency is high but its average looks fine. Which is the most useful next step?
qa.right: Look at the latency histogram and traces for the slow requests
wrong: Ignore p99 because the mean is good
Add more labels to every metric
qa.why: Averages hide tail latency; histograms and traces show where slow requests spend time.

qa.q: A storage bucket was found public. The team removed the public access. What else should they do?
qa.right: Check audit logs for access during the exposure and add a guardrail to block public buckets
wrong: Delete all logs to be safe
Make the bucket public again to compare
qa.why: Closing the hole does not tell you what was read; guardrails prevent a repeat.

qa.q: A cloud bill jumps overnight. Cost anomaly detection points at data transfer. Which cause should be checked first?
qa.right: A job or service moving large amounts of data across regions or out of the cloud
wrong: A tag added to a server
qa.why: Egress and cross-region transfer are common causes of sudden cost spikes.

qa.q: A team runs one pipeline job on a self-hosted runner that is reused for every pull request, including ones from forks. What is the main risk?
qa.right: Untrusted code can leave malware or steal secrets on a long-lived machine
wrong: Builds will be slower than on hosted runners
Pull requests will fail to merge
The cache will be too small
qa.why: Persistent self-hosted runners should not execute untrusted code; use ephemeral runners and restrict fork builds.

qa.q: A Terraform pipeline sometimes fails with a lock error after a cancelled run. What is the right response?
qa.right: Confirm no run is active, then release the stale lock deliberately
qa.why: A stale lock should be released with care after checking nobody is running; removing locking invites corruption.

qa.q: A company must recover its service in another region within 15 minutes with near-zero data loss. Which design fits best?
qa.right: Active-active or hot standby with continuous replication and a tested failover
wrong: Nightly backups copied to cold storage
A pilot light with data restored from last week
A single large instance in one zone
qa.why: Tight recovery time and point objectives need running capacity and continuous replication in the second region.

qa.q: A team wants engineers to create IAM roles for their own apps without being able to make themselves administrators. Which control fits?
qa.right: Require a permission boundary on every role they create
wrong: Give them the administrator policy and trust them
Share one admin role among all engineers
Ban role creation and use access keys
qa.why: The boundary caps what any role they create can do.

qa.q: A Kubernetes node is being drained for maintenance and all replicas of one service sit on it. What would have protected availability?
qa.right: A pod disruption budget and anti-affinity spreading replicas across nodes
qa.why: A PDB limits simultaneous voluntary disruption and spreading keeps replicas off one node.

qa.q: Metrics storage is growing fast after a developer added a request path label to a metric. What is the underlying problem?
qa.right: High cardinality from a label with many distinct values
wrong: The scrape target is too fast
qa.why: Each distinct label value creates a new series; unbounded values such as raw URLs multiply storage.

qa.q: A vendor offers a unique managed database that would save months of work but exists only on one cloud. What is the sound decision approach?
qa.right: Weigh the delivery benefit against exit cost and record the lock-in as an accepted risk
wrong: Reject any proprietary service on principle
Build the same service yourself on virtual machines
qa.why: Lock-in is a trade-off to be chosen deliberately, not an absolute.

qa.q: What does this Dockerfile instruction do?
qa.right: Copies the files from the build context into the image's /app directory
wrong: Runs the app at container start
Pulls an image from the registry
Mounts the host's /app directory at runtime
qa.why: COPY adds files to the image at build time.

qa.q: What does this Kubernetes manifest declare?
qa.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: web }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { app: web }
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: example/web:1.0
qa.right: A deployment keeping three identical pods running
wrong: A job that runs three times
A stateful set with three disks
qa.why: replicas sets the desired pod count; the controller maintains it.

qa.q: What is the effect of this container setting?
qa.code:
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 250m
    memory: 256Mi
  limits:
    memory: 512Mi
qa.right: The scheduler uses it to place the pod, while the limit caps usage
wrong: It reserves the resources only for other pods
It grants the pod a stable name
qa.why: A request guides scheduling; the limit is the cap.

qa.q: What does this PromQL expression compute?
qa.right: The per-second rate of requests over the last five minutes
wrong: The total number of requests ever
qa.why: rate() on a counter gives the per-second increase averaged over the window.

qa.q: A Terraform file uses this block. What does it do?
qa.right: Creates one resource per entry, keyed by name
wrong: Creates a single resource with five copies
Runs a script on the server
qa.why: for_each keys instances by name, so removing one leaves the others untouched.

qa.q: A GitHub Actions job needs a database for integration tests. What does this configuration provide?
qa.code:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      db:
        image: postgres
        ports: ["5432:5432"]
qa.right: A Postgres service container available to the job for its duration
wrong: A cache of the test results
A secret containing the database password
qa.why: Service containers start alongside the job and are discarded afterwards.

qa.q: Which line pins this third-party action to an exact version of its code?
qa.right: uses: org/action@a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0
qa.why: A full commit SHA cannot be moved; branches and tags can.

qa.q: What does this security-group style rule allow?
qa.right: Inbound HTTPS from anywhere
qa.why: Port 443 over TCP from 0.0.0.0/0 is open to the internet.

qa.q: What does this ingress-like rule risk if applied to a database?
qa.right: Exposing the database port to the entire internet
qa.why: Database ports should be limited to the application's security group, not open to the world.

qa.q: This Kubernetes policy is applied in a namespace. What does it do?
qa.code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
qa.right: Denies all inbound traffic to every pod in the namespace
qa.why: An empty pod selector with no ingress rules is a default-deny for ingress; other policies then add allowances.

qa.q: On our production VPS, which program restarts a crashed Node app?
qa.right: PM2
qa.why: PM2 supervises the process and revives it after a reboot once pm2 save has been run.

qa.q: Why does gglearn only allow Cloudflare to connect to its origin?
qa.right: To stop anyone bypassing Cloudflare and spoofing the X-Forwarded-For header
wrong: To remove the need for Apache
qa.why: The app reads the client address from X-Forwarded-For, which is trustworthy only when traffic comes through Cloudflare.

qa.q: A teammate says our infrastructure is managed with Terraform. What is accurate?
qa.right: No .tf files exist in the repos searched; Terraform is only a catalogued integration
wrong: Terraform builds the VPS for gglearn
Terraform runs the gglearn deploy workflow
qa.why: The rule is to say run, configured, catalogued or absent; Terraform is absent.

qa.q: A Moksy container exits with code 0 and stays down. Which restart policy would have prevented that?
qa.right: restart: unless-stopped
qa.why: on-failure only restarts after non-zero exit codes, so a clean exit is never retried.

qa.q: gglearn's deploy.sh polls the local app after restarting it. What happens if it never returns 200?
qa.right: The deploy is marked as failed
wrong: The workflow ignores it and succeeds
qa.why: The script polls up to ten times and fails the deploy; it does not roll back by itself.

qa.q: Someone proposes moving three small apps from the single VPS to Kubernetes because it is standard. What is the best response?
qa.right: Keep Compose and PM2 for now and revisit when service count or scaling needs grow
wrong: Move immediately because Kubernetes is always better
Move only the database to Kubernetes
Rewrite the apps first, then decide
qa.why: Kubernetes pays off with many services needing automatic scaling and healing; for a few apps it adds operating cost.

qa.q: gglearn's deploy workflow has no tests. Which improvement gives the largest safety gain with the least change?
qa.right: Add lint and test steps before the deploy step
wrong: Raise the number of health-poll attempts
qa.why: A failing check before deploy stops bad code reaching production.

qa.q: Where do we use Nginx?
qa.right: Inside Moksy's dashboard container as a static file server
wrong: As the reverse proxy on the VPS
As the load balancer for Kubernetes
qa.why: The VPS uses Apache; Nginx appears only in the dashboard image.
